change.title: pr-2-flat
change.description: Optimize spans buffer insertion with eviction during insert
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator breaks on the datetime key it is used with
findings.body: The audit log endpoint uses this paginator with `order_by="-datetime"` (organization_auditlogs.py:79-80). `get_item_key` copies `Paginator.get_item_key`, so it calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on a `datetime` and raises `TypeError`. That happens inside `build_cursor` (cursors.py:258-265) for any page that has results. `value_from_cursor` hands back the raw integer cursor value, and `build_queryset` puts it straight into `datetime <= %s` (paginator.py:119-126), so a follow-up cursor builds an invalid timestamp-vs-integer comparison. Result: any superuser or global-access member who sends `?optimized_pagination=true` gets a 500. If this paginator stays, it needs `DateTimePaginator`'s key and cursor conversion (paginator.py:230-241), for example by subclassing `DateTimePaginator`.

findings.title: The 'negative offset' feature can only fail, and the comments claim otherwise
findings.body: `Cursor.from_string` accepts a negative offset (cursors.py:59). This branch then runs `queryset[cursor.offset:stop]` with it. Django QuerySets reject negative indexing with `ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported.")`, so the request ends in a 500. The comments say Django 'properly handles negative slicing automatically' and that this 'enables access to data beyond normal pagination bounds… safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level'. The first is false. The second describes a bypass of pagination bounds as the intended behaviour. Remove the branch and clamp `start_offset` to 0. A negative cursor offset should be a 400, not something the paginator tries to honour.

findings.title: `organization_context.member` can be None, so the audit log endpoint can now 500 for every request
findings.body: `RpcUserOrganizationContext.member` is `RpcOrganizationMember | None` (organizations/services/organization/model.py:346). `enable_advanced` is computed on every request, not only when `optimized_pagination=true` is set. So any caller that passes `OrganizationAuditPermission` without a membership and without `user.is_superuser` now gets `AttributeError` before pagination runs. Examples are a legacy API key with `org:write`, where `request.user` is anonymous. Before this change, these callers got the normal audit log. Compute the flag only inside the `use_optimized` branch, and guard `member is not None`.

findings.title: Gate uses `user.is_superuser` instead of `is_active_superuser(request)`
findings.body: Elsewhere this codebase checks superuser privilege with `is_active_superuser(request)`, which requires an active superuser session; see OrganizationAuditPermission at api/bases/organization.py:124. `request.user.is_superuser` is true for a superuser account even without an elevated session. The path it unlocks is currently broken (see the other findings). Still, if it is kept, gate it the same way as the permission class.

findings.title: BasePaginator comment says negative offsets are allowed and safe
findings.body: Every paginator subclass shares this change. For `is_prev` cursors, a negative offset still goes into `queryset[offset:stop]`, and Django raises `ValueError`, the same as before this change. Only next-page cursors get clamped. The comment ('allow negative offsets… the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions') describes behaviour that does not exist. Either clamp both directions or drop the comment. The same goes for the comment added at utils/cursors.py:26-27.

findings.title: Switching segment keys from SET to ZSET has no migration for keys already in Redis
findings.body: Segment keys `span-buf:s:*` that the old code wrote are SETs, and they live up to `redis_ttl` (3600 s, buffer.py:151). After deploy, `ZADD` (buffer.py:197), `ZCARD`/`ZUNIONSTORE` here, and `ZSCAN` in `_load_segment_data` (buffer.py:434) all fail with WRONGTYPE on those keys. The pipeline raises, so `process_batch`/the flusher fail repeatedly until the old keys expire. While old and new consumers run side by side, the old code's `SADD`/`SSCAN` hit the new ZSETs the same way. Use a new key prefix, or handle the WRONGTYPE case.

findings.title: Spans over 1000 are dropped silently, and `max_segment_spans` is now dead
findings.body: Before, an oversized segment was skipped with a metric and an error log (`segment_span_count_exceeded`, now removed from buffer.py:449). Now `ZPOPMIN` discards the earliest-ending spans with no metric, no log, and nothing in the script's return value. The 1000 is hardcoded, while `SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans` (buffer.py:150,158) is still accepted but read nowhere. Pass the limit as an ARGV, return the evicted count, and emit a metric in `process_spans`.

findings.title: ZUNIONSTORE sums the scores of duplicate members
findings.body: `ZUNIONSTORE` defaults to `AGGREGATE SUM`. If the same payload ends up in both keys, for example a redelivered Kafka message, its score becomes the sum of two end timestamps. That puts it at the top of the ranking, so the eviction at lines 62-63 never removes it. Add `AGGREGATE MAX` to both calls (lines 47 and 53).

findings.title: Redirect depth limit cut 10x and its explanation removed
findings.body: The loop limit drops from 10000 to 1000, and the comment explaining the consequence ('segment trees of depth N may not be joined together correctly') is deleted. The PR body does not mention the change. Keep the comment, with the new number.

findings.title: No test covers the new eviction or the new paginator
findings.body: The test changes only add `end_timestamp_precise=1700000000.0` to existing fixtures, with the same value everywhere. Nothing covers the 1000-span cap, which spans `ZPOPMIN` evicts (ordered by end timestamp), merges across keys, or `OptimizedCursorPaginator`/`optimized_pagination`. A test of any of these would have caught the datetime `TypeError`.

contracts.before_after: DateTimePaginator turns datetimes into millisecond ints for the key and back to datetimes for the cursor; OptimizedCursorPaginator does neither
contracts.visible_effect: 500 TypeError from math.floor(datetime) inside build_cursor for any page with results
contracts.failure_mode: Crash on every non-empty page; negative-offset cursors raise Django ValueError

contracts.action: Compute enable_advanced on every audit log request
contracts.before_after: Before: no member access. After: dereferences member, which may be None
contracts.visible_effect: AttributeError 500 for callers without a membership who are not superusers
contracts.open_question: Which auth types (API keys, staff) reach this endpoint with member None and is_superuser False?

contracts.action: Span segment storage moved to ZSET with eviction at 1000
contracts.equivalent_path: Earlier flush-time skip in _load_segment_data based on max_segment_spans
contracts.before_after: Before: an oversized segment was dropped whole, with a metric and log. After: oldest spans evicted silently at insert
contracts.visible_effect: Flushed segments are missing spans, with no signal
contracts.failure_mode: WRONGTYPE errors on SET keys left over from before deploy

summary: The PR body describes only the spans-buffer change. The PR also adds an `OptimizedCursorPaginator` for audit logs that cannot work: its key function calls math.floor on a datetime, so every non-empty page returns a 500. Its 'negative offset' branch either crashes in Django or, per its own comments, is meant to bypass pagination bounds. The endpoint also dereferences a possibly-None member on every request. On the spans side: the SET to ZSET switch has no handling for keys already in Redis; spans over 1000 are evicted silently with a hardcoded limit, which leaves max_segment_spans unused; and there are no tests for the new behaviour.
